subject: Demo recap — latency & throughput fitment, GPU reckoning
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@sagelabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap — latency & throughput fitment, GPU reckoning

Hi Elena / Sage infra team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and a proposed path to validate the SLOs you outlined. I wrote this to keep the follow-ups tightly scoped so we can get to an actual pilot quickly.

Key constraints you mentioned on the call:
- Target latency: 30–50 ms P95 for short-response paths (chat completion snippets).
- Burst throughput: up to ~200 qps sustained for 10–15 second windows; baseline ~100 qps.
- Concurrency requirement: up to 12 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions; many sessions will stream partial tokens.
- Streaming: required for partial outputs / streaming hints to UX.
- Typical prompt/response size: 40–80 tokens request, 60–250 tokens response (variable).

Immediate ask from Redwood to validate fit:
1) Confirm which path is priority: low-latency short responses (30ms P95) vs higher throughput with slightly larger latencies (50ms P95).
2) Share a representative prompt set (or point us to the SLO spreadsheet) and a peak-load window we can replay.
3) Preferred pilot timeline (2–3 week run vs 48-hour smoke-bench).

Initial sizing notes (high-level, opinionated):
- H100-80GB: best raw latency at high concurrency with large batch support; good for heavy KV cache workloads and streaming.
- A100-80GB: solid all-rounder; slightly higher P95 vs H100 at identical concurrency but lower cost on reserved nodes.
- L4 / equivalent 48GB inference GPUs: much cheaper, good for embeddings / smaller models, but higher latency variance under bursty streaming.

Proposal: a small pilot using reserved capacity (2 GPUs) with the following plan:
- Benchmark matrix: 30/50/100 qps with 1/6/12 concurrent streaming sessions across the three GPU SKUs above.
- Measure: P50/P95/P99 latencies, tokens/sec, KV cache hit delta, and tail latency under cold-start of KV cache.
- Deliverables: SLO matrix populated (we'll start the SLO sheet), raw bench logs, and a recommendation for the reserved slab size for production.

Attachments: I attached a starter SLO matrix and a short GPU benchmark summary (stubs below).

Attachments:
- slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO rows we plan to populate)
- gpu_benchmarks_summary.pdf (high-level expected trade-offs)

Next steps I can take this week:
- Stand up bench harness and an initial smoke run (48 hours) if you can give us a small sample prompt set.
- Schedule a 30-min bench sync with your infra folks to wire in streaming hooks (trace ids, partial tokens).

Thanks,

Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
l: +1 (415) 555-0124

> - Priority path: the short-response UX is the current gating factor — 30ms P95 for the fastest flows is ideal. If necessary, we can relax to 40ms for longer responses.
> - Prompt set: attaching an anonymized sample set (~200 prompts), average request ~55 tokens, responses 80–180 tokens. We'll upload to the secure link you suggested after NDA confirmation.
> - Pilot timeline: we can start a 72-hour smoke-bench next week (preferred) and then extend to a 2-week pilot if smoke results look good.
>
> Constraints to call out:

> - We need streaming to be functional end-to-end (partial tokens + session affinity) during the smoke run.
>
> Can you give an example of expected P95 numbers for each GPU SKU for our prompt sizes so we can set internal expectations? Also confirm what telemetry you need from our side (traces, request ids, user ids).
>

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@sagelabs.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Demo recap — latency & throughput fitment, GPU reckoning

Elena — thanks for the quick clarification. A few concrete numbers + a practical minimal-scope bench plan to respect Sage's pilot budget: 

Rough expected P95 ballpark (50–180 token responses, single model family we discussed):
- H100-80GB (reserved, tuned): ~22–35 ms P95 at 30–50 qps with 6 concurrent streams; ~28–45 ms at 100 qps depending on batching.
- A100-80GB (reserved): ~30–50 ms P95 at 30–50 qps; ~40–70 ms at 100 qps with elevated tail.
- L4-class 48GB inference GPU: ~45–110 ms P95 depending on batch patterns; better for cost but riskier for tight 30ms targets.

Pilot (budget-conscious smoke run):
- Phase 1 (48–72 hr smoke, 1 reserved GPU): run 3 measured scenarios at 30 qps with 3 concurrent streams, 60 qps burst test, and a streaming session stability test.
- Phase 2 (if smoke passes): scale to 2 reserved GPUs and run the full matrix (30/50/100 qps, concurrency 1/6/12).

Telemetry we need from Sage for benching:
- Representative prompt set (anonymized) — you mentioned this.
- A single stable endpoint and a short list of request headers we can annotate (x-sage-session-id, x-request-id).
- Optionally a synthetic user-id map for session-affinity tests.

HubSpot / scheduling: I opened the deal (link below) and added a scheduling block next Thurs for a 30-min bench sync. If smoke budget is constrained we can run the smoke bench on a smaller instance and emulate higher throughput via concurrent clients rather than adding reserved GPUs.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/78321

Action items for Redwood (I will own):
- Stand up the bench harness and a baseline A100 vs H100 smoke run (48–72 hrs) using your prompt set.
- Share the populated SLO matrix after smoke run and a recommendation for reserved slab size (1 vs 2 GPUs).

Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Elena — quick operational next steps and commitments from our side: 

1) We'll start Phase 1 smoke run next Monday assuming we receive the anonymized prompt set by end of day Friday. If NDA is needed for the data transfer, please flag and we'll route through Legal.
2) Redwood will instrument streaming traces and provide a lightweight client script for your infra team to validate session affinity.
3) We'll deliver a filled SLO matrix and the smoke-run bench report (P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and a short set of tail-case notes) within 5 business days of smoke completion.

Deliverable attachments (placeholders): slo_matrix.xlsx, gpu_benchmarks_summary.pdf

If the smoke run shows the H100 comfortably hitting ~30ms P95 for your short-path flow, we'll propose a 2-GPU reserved slab for production with autoscaling guardrails. If A100 meets your budget and latency tolerances we'll document expected cost/latency tradeoffs.

I'll book the bench sync for Thursday 10–10:30am PT (tentative) — please accept or propose an alternate.

Thanks and talk soon,

Ben Carter
